_about: The loose bodies a level starts with AT REST, because the original shows them so from its first frame (planning step 152's amendment,
R3b fix 1; sim/Resting). The key is the level's file name without its extension, `bodies` the nodes' names in its .tscn: each is put to
sleep where the level places it, with the position it sleeps at, as the engine itself writes a body that has been still long enough
(PhysicsSystem's sleep test), so it wakes by the engine's own rules - a body it touches that moves, or the port moving it (a portal's exit).
WHY a body needs this. A pile of a heavy body on a light one, resting on corners, is not held by the engine's eight solver iterations: the
stone of 3-12 (1.131, the .ent's density over its 30 radius) rests on the small crate's corner (0.144) and the column's, presses the crate
sideways along the contact's normal every tick, and the crate creeps off its ledge from tick 4 with the stone after it (R3b fix 1: the
pair drifts at an equal weight too, 154 -> 144.6 in 180 ticks, and at 2 m/s^2 of gravity, a fifth of the world's, the stone is off its
perch by tick 300). Box2D holds it, as the original's stills show. A body listed here is what the original shows and the engine cannot keep.
Only a pile named from a still of the original belongs here; the others that are awake at tick 420 (test_mp_timebase's list) are not
listed, because no still of theirs has been compared.
_wake_reach_px: How near a sleeping body must lie to a body the port is about to move away (a portal's entry) for it to wake with it. A GUESS (_guess true):
no number of the original's decides it. MEASURED on 3-12's route (R3b fix 1): the stone cradled in the nook lies 1.95 units off the crate's
corner on the port's geometry (a circle of radius 30 whose centre is 31.95 from the corner), and the route wins on tick 624 for every reach
from 2 to the 40 tried and not for 1.8 or less, so 6 is a few units of margin over that gap, not a knife-edge. WHY it wakes at all: the stone of
3-12 is held in a nook inside a permanent antiportal's field by the small crate, and the way to free it is to take the crate away through a
portal - which only works if the stone then rolls. Box2D 2.2.1 (the original's) wakes both bodies of a contact when it ends (b2Contact::Update,
b2Contact.cpp:210-214, and b2Contact::Destroy, :105-109), so in the original a stone asleep on a crate that goes is woken as the contact goes;
the engine wakes a sleeper only when a contact begins or a neighbour stirs, so the port supplies the original's rule where it moves a body itself.
